Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, Madrid) for the name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the registered office for final inscription.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Consolidated Spanish Capital Companies Act, Ley de Sociedades de Capital – LSC), Articles 20–23 (incorporation formalities), 22 as amended by Ley 18/2022 (minimum capital abolished), 27 (legal reserve), 33 (legal personality upon registration), 62 (registration of deed), and 209–211 (appointment of administrators); Ley 19/2013, Article 33 (obligatory Interest Groups Register).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) executed before a Spanish Notary, presented to the Registro Mercantil Provincial together with Form D-1 for registration and proof of settlement of the transfer tax (ITP-AJD).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 42 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Under Ley 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), the minimum €3,000 capital quota for S.L. is abolished. The incorporation deed may provide a statutory capital from €1, fully subscribed and paid in cash at the time of execution. The legal reserve regime (Art. 27 LSC) nevertheless requires allocation of 20% of annual profits until the paid-in capital plus legal reserve reaches €3,000. Bank escrow account rules apply only to non-cash contributions; cash contributions are evidenced by the notarial statement of payment.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) issued by the municipal technical inspection service or an authorized collaboration entity; structural load and occupancy clearance for premises over 300 m² or with a capacity exceeding 50 persons; workplace safety and health surveillance plan (Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales) covering the office, ergonomics, electrical installation, and emergency evacuation; and municipal accessibility clearance (Real Decreto 505/2007).

Paid-in capital rule: Under Ley 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), the minimum €3,000 capital quota for S.L. is abolished. The incorporation deed may provide a statutory capital from €1, fully subscribed and paid in cash at the time of execution. The legal reserve regime (Art. 27 LSC) nevertheless requires allocation of 20% of annual profits until the paid-in capital plus legal reserve reaches €3,000. Bank escrow account rules apply only to non-cash contributions; cash contributions are evidenced by the notarial statement of payment.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/

E-government filing portal

A foreign entity establishing a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must first obtain a N.I.F. (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for the company. The procedure is: (1) apply for a provisional CIF/NIF via the AEAT before notarising the deed of incorporation, or alternatively obtain a definitive NIF after registration in the Mercantile Registry; (2) file Form 036/037 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) to be registered in the Census of Economic Activities and obtain the definitive VAT identification number (NIF-IVA). For EU entities a valid EU VAT ID may suffice for intra-community operations, but for a branch or permanent establishment a Spanish NIF is mandatory. Bank account proof, notarised incorporation deed, and power of attorney are generally required; an online electronic certificate (certificado electrónico) is needed for digital filing.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation – Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada are separate taxable persons (contribuyentes del Impuesto sobre Sociedades) and are not pass-through entities. Profits are taxed at the corporate income tax rate (currently 25%, with 15% for newly created entities in the first two years of taxable profits under certain conditions). Shareholders are separately taxed on distributions. The entity is also a taxable person for VAT (IVA) purposes. — A foreign entity establishing a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must first obtain a N.I.F. (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for the company. The procedure is: (1) apply for a provisional CIF/NIF via the AEAT before notarising the deed of incorporation, or alternatively obtain a definitive NIF after registration in the Mercantile Registry; (2) file Form 036/037 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) to be registered in the Census of Economic Activities and obtain the definitive VAT identification number (NIF-IVA). For EU entities a valid EU VAT ID may suffice for intra-community operations, but for a branch or permanent establishment a Spanish NIF is mandatory. Bank account proof, notarised incorporation deed, and power of attorney are generally required; an online electronic certificate (certificado electrónico) is needed for digital filing.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation – Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada are separate taxable persons (contribuyentes del Impuesto sobre Sociedades) and are not pass-through entities. Profits are taxed at the corporate income tax rate (currently 25%, with 15% for newly created entities in the first two years of taxable profits under certain conditions). Shareholders are separately taxed on distributions. The entity is also a taxable person for VAT (IVA) purposes.

Available election forms

Under Spanish tax law there is no direct 'check-the-box' election. Relevant election mechanisms include: (a) the 'consolidaciôn fiscal' election available to groups of companies meeting the 70% shareholding threshold and other requirements (articles 67-77 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law 27/2014); (b) the option under article 61 of the same law to include or exclude certain tax credits and deductions; (c) the option for the general regime versus the simplified regime for small enterprises and the special regime for new entities (15% rate election); and (d) hybrid mismatch structuring is strictly constrained by the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) as transposed in the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law, with mandatory disclosure obligations for aggressive tax planning. A foreign shareholder cannot unilaterally elect to ignore the SL's legal personality for tax purposes.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

Spain does not require VAT registration solely on the basis of turnover for habitual entrepreneurs; registration is obligatory from the first taxable supply (no universal general exemption threshold comparable to the UK £85k). However, small businesses with an annual volume of operations not exceeding EUR 250,000 may elect the Simplified Regime (régimen simplificado), under which VAT liability is determined via module/flat-rate formulas. For non-established (foreign) suppliers selling to Spanish non-taxable persons in excess of €10,000 annually via electronic interfaces, the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) special regime may apply. For B2B services, reverse charge applies without registration if the recipient is registered; but for physical business presence or local operations, full Spanish NIF-IVA registration is mandatory.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods to third countries (outside the EU) are zero-rated (exempt with right to deduction) under article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, provided the goods physically leave the EU within the legally established periods and are supported by documentary evidence. Supplies of services directly connected to export of goods (e.g., logistics, packing) may also be zero-rated. Exemptions for intra-community supplies (article 25) apply when the buyer is registered with a valid EU VAT ID and goods are transported within the EU. Offshore services rendered by the Spanish SL to foreign clients are generally zero-rated if the place of supply is outside Spain (B2B under Article 69-70 of the VAT Law), provided the counterparty is a taxable person outside the EU or in another EU territory under reverse charge rules.

  • Documento Único Administrativo (DUA) / Single Administrative Document (SAD) – customs export declaration with the unique movement reference number (MRN)
  • Commercial invoice issued by the Spanish exporter (factura comercial)
  • Bill of Lading (B/L) or AWB (air waybill) evidencing physical departure of goods from EU customs territory
  • Delivery/acceptance proof including the recipient's signature, warehouse receipts, or customs stamped documents
  • Evidence of payment and Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de remesa de entrada) issued by the Spanish bank or SWIFT/MT103 confirmation for proof of receipt of foreign currency
  • For intra-community supplies: the customer's valid EU VAT registration number and periodic recapitulative statement (modelo 349)

Spain mandates electronic invoicing for B2B transactions through the 'Verifactura' system and the Crea y Crece law (Law 18/2022) effective from 2024 for business-to-business e-invoicing for entities with annual turnover over EUR 8 million, and later for all entities. The mandate requires structured electronic invoices (JSON/XML) with a digital fingerprint (hash) and end-to-end integrity, and the use of approved software providers. Real-time fiscal clearance (similar to Spanish 'TicketBAI' system) is already compulsory in the Basque Country and parts of Navarre; nationwide 'Verifactura' will require real-time reporting to AEAT or qualified software platforms. Foreign entities issuing invoices in Spain must comply with data content requirements (full NIF, invoice serial number, dates, base, tax amounts) and, where applicable, use qualified electronic signatures.

AEAT may retrospectively correct improperly zero-rated exports and recover unpaid VAT plus interest. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the tax avoided for 'infracción tributaria' (Tax Law General, ley 58/2003). In fraudulent export schemes, criminal tax fraud penalties under the Spanish Criminal Code apply, including imprisonment for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 (art. 305). Additionally, false or incomplete customs declarations attract customs penalties under Spanish Customs Law (Ley 19/2020), and the exporter may lose eligibility for simplification or suspension of registration. Substantiation documentation must be retained for four years plus, in practice, at least five years from the end of the filing period.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a Eurozone Member State and the euro is fully convertible. Under TFEU Articles 63–66, capital and payment movements between Spain, other EU Member States, and qualifying third countries are fully liberalised. No exchange-control approval is required for current-account transactions, dividend distributions, profit remittance, royalty payments, or liquidation proceeds. Profit repatriation from an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is permitted without convertibility restrictions, subject to corporate validation: audited financial statements where legally required, a shareholders' resolution confirming the dividend or reduction of capital, satisfaction of the capital-maintenance test, and no outstanding tax liabilities to the Agencia Tributaria. All transfers to non-residents above the annual statistical threshold of EUR 1,000,000 must be reported through the Banco de España's balance-of-payments declarations. Payments originating from or destined to non-cooperative tax jurisdictions or jurisdictions under FATF enhanced monitoring may receive additional AML scrutiny but remain legally convertible.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no statutory surrender requirements on export proceeds or service revenues in foreign currency. There is no mandatory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio to euro. Exporters and service providers may maintain collections in foreign-currency accounts or hedge them freely through authorised credit institutions. The Spanish SL is required to support any inward remittance from a non-resident with the underlying invoice, contract, and, where applicable, proof of service delivery, so that the receiving bank can satisfy anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening. Where the aggregate annual volume of transactions with non-residents exceeds EUR 1,000,000, the SL must file the corresponding statistical declaration with the Banco de España.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting jointly with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio, for foreign-investment registration and balance-of-payments statistical reporting.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Medium for EU-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) that hold a valid passport under PSD2 and are registered with the Banco de España or are operating through a branch; Low for offshore, non-EEA digital EMIs without a Spanish or EU banking licence. A non-EU EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to the Spanish SL unless it establishes a Spanish branch or partners with an EU-licensed payment institution. For the ISIC 7020 government-affairs lobbying activity, tier-1 credit institutions are recommended over EMI rails because of the statutory-licence requirement, enhanced PEP exposure, and the need for auditable correspondent-banking trails. When EMI rails are used, the SL must ensure that the EMI maintains a segregated safeguarding account and that incoming retainer wires can be traced to the ultimate client for AML and conflict-of-interest reviews.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-EU resident or is in a high-risk third country

Root cause: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-EU resident or is in a high-risk third country

Defense evidence: Apostilled corporate extract from the home registry, notarised UBO declaration, source-of-wealth statement, certified passport copies, EU tax-residence certificate or equivalent, a negative sanctions and PEP screening, and a corroborating legal opinion from the incorporating counsel.
Business scope is 'government affairs and lobbying' and directors may be treated as politically exposed persons (PEPs)

Root cause: Business scope is 'government affairs and lobbying' and directors may be treated as politically exposed persons (PEPs)

Defense evidence: Valid domestic lobbying registration licence or exemption certificate, documented client engagement contracts, detailed fee schedule, written compliance and conflicts-of-interest policies, anti-bribery training records, PEP clearance for all shareholders and directors, and a forensic accounting opinion confirming no capitation or corruption-linked revenue.
Outbound disbursements to foreign public-affairs consultants or sub-agents

Root cause: Outbound disbursements to foreign public-affairs consultants or sub-agents

Defense evidence: Executed consultancy agreements with clearly defined deliverables, KYC files and beneficial-ownership details of each payee, sanctions and adverse-media screening reports, timesheets or activity reports evidencing real services, tax invoices satisfying Spanish invoicing rules, and an authorised payment-matrix signed by two directors.
Substance mismatch between forecast retainer revenue and minimal staff or physical premises

Root cause: Substance mismatch between forecast retainer revenue and minimal staff or physical premises

Defense evidence: Lease agreement for registered office and administrative space in Spain, employment contracts plus social security registrations (alta en la Seguridad Social), corporate tax references and VAT filings, audited or internally prepared financial projections, and a bank reference letter from the source of capital.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

For inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders into the Spanish SL, the standard compliant rail is a SWIFT MT103 through a licensed credit institution. The sending bank must include the company's Spanish NIF, the beneficiary IBAN (starting 'ES'), and the SWIFT UETR for end-to-end traceability. The remittance narrative must state the purpose as 'Aportación de capital social / Capital increase' for equity injections or 'Préstamo entre empresas / Intercompany loan' for shareholder financing. Equity injections should be contemporaneous with the notarial deed of capital increase and the subsequent filing at the Mercantile Registry; if the investment exceeds EUR 3,000,000, or if the investor is a non-EU entity in a screened sector, the DGCIIN foreign-investment registration must be completed under applicable Spanish FDI rules. For operational retainer inflows, the incoming wire purpose code should be 'Servicios profesionales / Professional services' and the bank must hold a signed retainer contract and KYC file for the foreign client. All inbound wires must be accompanied by a currency declaration to the bank and, where applicable, a balance-of-payments statistical filing for annual flows above EUR 1,000,000.For outbound trade and service settlement, the SL will use SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for EU/EEA transactions of lower value, and SWIFT MT103 for international payments, especially retainer fees to foreign law firms, government-relations consultants, and trade-policy analysts. For USD-denominated payments, the correspondent clearing rail is typically Fedwire or CHIPS through the bank's US correspondents; for EUR, TARGET2 is used; and for other currencies the bank may use SWIFT gpi correspondent banking with continuous tracking. A commercial letter of credit is only appropriate where the underlying activity involves tangible goods, which is not the natural case for ISIC 7020 advisory and lobbying services; where required for ancillary procurements, it may be issued by a tier-1 bank with conformity documents such as invoices, insurance certificates, and customs declarations. To prevent compliance holds, each outgoing MT103 must carry the purpose description 'Professional services — government affairs consultancy', supported by the invoice, the contract, and the recipient's bank and KYC details. The SL should maintain a register of all outward wires with the corresponding UETR and SWIFT gpi tracker.Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP deliverable FX forwards executed with a Banco de España-authorised credit institutionFX swaps (swap de divisas) for short-term treasury liquidity conversion and refinancing of currency exposuresCross-currency swaps for long-dated foreign-currency retainer receivables or intercompany loan exposuresNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies where no onshore deliverable forward existsFX options and collars entered into under MiFID II suitability rules for genuine commercial hedging, with no speculative leverage

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) that hold a valid passport under PSD2 and are registered with the Banco de España or are operating through a branch; Low for offshore, non-EEA digital EMIs without a Spanish or EU banking licence. A non-EU EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to the Spanish SL unless it establishes a Spanish branch or partners with an EU-licensed payment institution. For the ISIC 7020 government-affairs lobbying activity, tier-1 credit institutions are recommended over EMI rails because of the statutory-licence requirement, enhanced PEP exposure, and the need for auditable correspondent-banking trails. When EMI rails are used, the SL must ensure that the EMI maintains a segregated safeguarding account and that incoming retainer wires can be traced to the ultimate client for AML and conflict-of-interest reviews.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Entities with net turnover ≥ €10 million must prepare Master File and Local File. For entities below threshold, documentation required only if related-party transactions exceed €250,000 per counterparty or €1 million in aggregate. Additionally, all transactions with tax havens must be documented regardless of amount.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) but applies general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles. For tax residency, entities must have real economic activity (premises, employees, management) in Spain. Treaty benefits may be denied if no substance. Lobbying activities must be substantiated with contracts, invoices, and evidence of actual services.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax evaded, plus late payment interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding €120,000 per year, leading to imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and fine of up to 6 times the evaded amount.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts if they caused or contributed to the evasion. Criminal liability extends to directors, with potential travel bans and asset freezes.
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: Reclassification of income, denial of treaty benefits, and imposition of 25% penalty on deemed income. Administrative dissolution of the company and cancellation of tax registration.

Director personal liability: Directors may be held personally liable for corporate tax liabilities if they knowingly operated a sham entity. Travel bans and prohibition on holding directorships for up to 10 years.
AML (Anti-Money Laundering)

Statutory sanction: Fines up to €150,000 for serious infractions, and up to €1.5 million for very serious infractions. Criminal charges for money laundering with imprisonment of 1 to 6 years and fines.

Director personal liability: Directors can be criminally liable for AML breaches, with personal fines and imprisonment. Travel bans and restrictions on managing financial entities.
